clue.text: Standing up to attack of illness very well

parts.note: standing up to an enemy is fighting it
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing or epilepsy

explanation.surface: A patient resisting a bout of sickness is doing remarkably well.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in peak physical condition is an idiom for being in excellent health.

clue.text: Fond of pasta for starters? Here's macaroni

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, here the initial letter of each word

explanation.surface: A pasta lover gives his recommendation: macaroni.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaroni is an old word for an eighteenth-century dandy who affected Continental fashions, not just pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroni was a fashionable dandy of the 1770s, so a vain overdressed man.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Cheddar in Somerset has a famous ravine

explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself, and Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England.

clue.text: Produced a parody and became a success

definitions.meaning: suddenly to become popular, as a career might

explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to imitate them, and a career that soars is said to have done so.

clue.text: Myself, I'm top of the pops

definitions.meaning: a colloquial term for oneself, looking after your own interests
the best-selling record in the charts

explanation.definitionFit: Looking after oneself is an idiom for putting myself first, and the chart-topping record holds the first spot.

clue.text: Place for discussion of uplifted: spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Somewhere to talk about cheered-up souls.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum was a Roman public square for debate, now any assembly or medium for discussion.

clue.text: Strong material making a recurrent sound

definitions.meaning: a hard-wearing cotton or linen fabric for mattresses
clicking regularly, as a clock does

explanation.definitionFit: Tough striped fabric for mattress covers has this name, and a clock does it with each repeated click.

clue.text: Greetings associated with man …

definitions.meaning: plural of the informal salutation hi
the possessive pronoun for something belonging to a male

explanation.definitionFit: Hellos said casually are hi's, and the masculine possessive pronoun marks what belongs to a man.

clue.text: Hesitates over small person's needlework

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to hem and haw is to hesitate
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A dithering little person struggles with sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is informal British for a tiny person; the 's of 'person's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemstitch is a decorative stitch used in sewing hems, a type of needlework.

clue.text: Camping equipment 'left inside leaking container.

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another

parts.note: seeping means leaking slowly
a bag is a container

explanation.surface: Camping kit has been abandoned in a holed holdall.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded sack for sleeping in is standard kit when camping.

clue.text: … a one-time entertainer

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds per (a) head
one-time means earlier or former

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the greeting comes from a showman whose days on stage are over.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who acts, sings or plays for an audience is an entertainer.

clue.text: Search eastern valley

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A hunt through a valley lying to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short steep valley, a word common in the south-west of England.

clue.text: Different version of Eeyore's Blot on the landscape

indicators.note: a different version of the letters means they are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A twist on the gloomy donkey from Winnie-the-Pooh turns out to spoil the view.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive counts as a letter here: the seven letters of the donkey's name with its S are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that spoils a view is a common idiomatic sense of blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Meet a priest working in New York

indicators.note: working means operating or being reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Meeting a cleric on duty in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the wordplay to the definition; the state of New York is nicknamed after its imperial ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: New York State's nickname refers to its wealth and power, so the name stands for it.

clue.text: Scholar, interested in the origin of '. platforms, developed one such at sea

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
to be into something is to be keen on or interested in it

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An academic keen on how platforms began came up with a design for a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one such' points back to 'platforms': the definition is a platform at sea. 'developed' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A maintop is the platform at the head of a sailing ship's mainmast, so a platform found at sea.

clue.text: Academic concealing old evidence,

indicators.note: something concealing another holds it inside itself

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic

explanation.surface: A university teacher hides some ancient evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence strong enough to establish a fact.

clue.text: Maker of prostheses' starts off humorous catalogue

indicators.note: starts off means each word loses its first letter

parts.note: jocular means humorous
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A firm making artificial limbs begins with a jokey brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' removes the first letter from both JOCULAR and LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocularist makes artificial eyes, which are prostheses.

clue.text: Name attached to Argonaut disturbed primate

indicators.note: one piece is attached to the end of another
letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A name is pinned on one of Jason's crew, who has been upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges ARGONAUT into ORANGUTA; 'attached to' then adds N at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, a primate.

clue.text: Who invented a frame? Noah?

definitions.meaning: Richard ... patented the water frame for spinning cotton
a wright is a builder, so Noah was a builder of the ark

explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright invented the water frame, and Noah as builder of the ark was an ark-wright.

clue.text: Oil worker's heavy caress

parts.note: a heavy sea or a heavy handling is a rough one
to neck is to kiss and caress

explanation.surface: A man on the oil rig is clumsy with his embraces.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'worker's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughneck is a labourer on an oil rig, as well as a slang word for a rowdy person.

clue.text: Unfortunate tramp's last boarding tow boat

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to hale is an old word for haul or tow

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a boat

explanation.surface: A down-and-out who has just climbed aboard a tug boat is out of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: P, the final letter of 'tramp', goes inside HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky, without hap or good fortune.

clue.text: In India, Sir Henry, runs into recurrent prejudice

indicators.note: one piece runs into another by entering it
recurrent is read as running back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a bias is a prejudice
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: In India, Sir Henry finds himself facing persistent prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrent' turns BIAS into SAIB, and H goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was the respectful form of address used in colonial India, the equivalent of sir.

clue.text: Animal cross that's lively at first

parts.note: to span a river is to cross it
i.e. is short for id est, that is

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A creature crossbred to be lively from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of dog, so an animal.

clue.text: Run 'second-vehicle

parts.note: a camper is a motor vehicle fitted out for living in

explanation.surface: The second car in a race or service.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly and playfully, like a child or small animal.

clue.text: More than one spoke with leader — in Rome 2002 years ago

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

parts.note: the puzzle dates from about 2004, so 2002 years earlier was AD 2, which in Roman numerals is AD II

explanation.surface: A multi-spoked wheel ridden by a chief in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' hints at Roman numerals; 'with' links R to the date AD II.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokes of a wheel run from centre to rim like radii of a circle, the plural of radius.

clue.text: Inconsiderate driver drove noisily to corner.

indicators.note: noisily means the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: drove means rode, travelled in a vehicle
to hog something is to corner or monopolise it

explanation.surface: A selfish motorist roared loudly round a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a driver who selfishly takes up more than a fair share of the road.

clue.text: Henry 'overcame mother in game

indicators.note: read as over came, the first piece came over the second in this down clue

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Henry beat his mother at a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which pieces jump across squares, a forerunner of Chinese chequers.

clue.text: Aware of a bad setback

indicators.note: set back is read as put in reverse, so the word is turned round

parts.note: bad and evil are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone conscious of a nasty reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns EVIL into LIVE; 'of' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive to something is to be alert to it, so alive can mean conscious or sensitive.

clue.text: Small bloomer. — give to old drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiny mistake: offer the old soak a tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog-violet is a small wild flower, and a flowering plant is a bloomer.

clue.text: Oriental-sounding piece of attire

indicators.note: sounding means heard aloud rather than seen

parts.note: Thai means from Thailand, in the Orient

explanation.surface: A garment that sounds Eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is worn round the neck, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Get to have a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Something that gets to you is said to be eating you, and to dine is to take food.

clue.text: Glitter — I can tell it's moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift into new positions

explanation.surface: A gleaming display that someone senses is in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To scintillate is to sparkle or flash, as gems do.
